name: Jawaharlal Nehru
description: India’s first prime minister, associated with parliamentary democracy, secular government and economic planning.
scope: Public positions and conduct during the specified period; this represents the individual rather than all party members or citizens.

axes.brief: Universal franchise and parliamentary competition framed the republic.
axes.counter: Preventive detention and dismissal of Kerala’s government qualify democratic decentralisation.

reasons.8: The 1949 Cabinet explicitly avoided a national Communist Party ban, while state bans and security repression were justified by alleged violence. Those actions do not establish permission to exclude parties merely for political positions; qualified disagreement is more likely.

axes.brief: Constitutional liberties coexisted with preventive detention and speech restrictions.
axes.counter: Democratic rhetoric is not proof of opposition to all coercive public-order measures.

axes.brief: Plural national identity and minority recognition supported cultural coexistence.
axes.counter: National unity and common institutions still constrained community autonomy.

axes.brief: Partition refugees and equal citizenship shaped a managed national admissions context.
axes.counter: Modern general settlement rights and welfare systems are uncertain translations.

axes.brief: Non-alignment and diplomacy coexisted with military action in Goa and border defence.
axes.counter: Avoiding blocs did not mean complete pacifism or no military capability.

axes.brief: International cooperation and anti-colonial solidarity coexisted with sovereign non-alignment.
axes.counter: UN participation did not amount to surrendering all national legal authority.

axes.brief: Heavy public-sector industry anchored the mixed economy.
axes.counter: Private and village industries remained; not all ownership was nationalised.

axes.brief: Import substitution and industrial protection supported national development.
axes.counter: Trade and international assistance still contributed to industrialisation.

axes.brief: Five-Year Plans directed investment and strategic industries.
axes.counter: Planning included public consultation and private production rather than universal identical quotas.

axes.brief: Land reform and social opportunity aimed to reduce entrenched inequality.
axes.counter: Implementation and resources constrained equalisation; a modern wealth-transfer scheme remains inferred.

axes.brief: Secular state policy and civil marriage coexisted with religious personal law.
axes.counter: Personal-law accommodation complicates claims of entirely uniform civil family law.

axes.brief: Gender and family-law reform challenged some customary institutions.
axes.counter: Modern same-sex and gender-identity claims are outside the explicit period record.

axes.brief: Scientific institutions, dams and industrial development were major priorities.
axes.counter: Scientific temper does not prove willingness to approve untested human enhancement.

axes.brief: A strong national centre guided planning and maintained unity.
axes.counter: Linguistic states and local development programmes preserved regional roles.

axes.brief: Education and changing social relationships were central to his account of development.
axes.counter: Specific genetic comparisons across psychological traits remain undocumented.
axes.gap: These are tentative analogical causal judgments; scientific modernisation is not itself a position on the relative contribution of heredity.
